lines.text: Tides come from a pull that gets weaker with the cube of the distance.
lines.cue: caption: PULL FALLS WITH DISTANCE CUBED

lines.text: Today the Moon is about three hundred eighty-four thousand kilometers away.
Lower it to the space station's height, and its center is about eighty-five hundred kilometers from the Earth's center.
lines.cue: caption: ABOUT 8,500 KM FROM THE CENTER

lines.text: Cube that change in distance, and the tidal pull comes out about ninety-two thousand times today's.
That's our own sum from a simple model, not a measured tide.
lines.cue: caption: OUR SUM, NOT A MEASURED TIDE

lines.text: But the Moon is a ball three thousand four hundred seventy-six kilometers across. Its near side is pulled more than twice as hard as its far side.
lines.cue: caption: NEAR SIDE: MORE THAN 2x THE FAR SIDE

lines.text: So would the Moon hold together?
The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
